subject: Dedicated reservation options and ramp plan for NeuraHealth predictive API
messages:
From: Elliot Morris <elliot@neurahealth.com>
To: Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.inference>
Cc: NeuraHealth Procurement <procurement@neurahealth.com>
Date: Tue, 01 Dec 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Dedicated capacity sizing for predictive API

Hi Aditya,

Thanks for the demo last week — the NeuraHealth infra team liked the latency profile. We are starting procurement planning and need a concrete set of reservation options to present to our finance and infra committees. High-level inputs:~
- Peak ingest ~1,200 short-text requests/sec (99% requests ~<1k tokens), 10% of requests need 16k-32k context (longer context).~
- Target p95 generation latency: <= 150ms for short requests, <= 400ms for long-context batches (where possible).~
- Expected steady growth: 15% month-over-month for first 6 months after go-live.
- Preferred hardware: H100 or equivalent (we can consider A100 where necessary).
- Procurement timeline: decision by mid-Dec, contract signed by end of Jan.

Can you put together 2–3 reservation paths (e.g., conservative baseline, staircase/ramped, frontloaded) with suggested cluster size, minimum committed GPUs, burst/overflow options, and a rough monthly cost range? Also include a suggested ramp schedule tied to deal milestones and a canary approach for month 1.

If you can include any assumptions you used (QPS mapping to GPU counts, batching assumptions), that will help speed approvals.

Thanks — copying Procurement to keep them in the loop.

Best,
Elliot Morris
VP Product, NeuraHealth
elliot@neurahealth.com

From: Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.inference>
To: Elliot Morris <elliot@neurahealth.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.inference>, Lauren Bishop <lauren@redwood.inference>, NeuraHealth Procurement <procurement@neurahealth.com>
Date: Tue, 01 Dec 2026 14:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity sizing for predictive API

Elliot — thanks for the clear inputs. We've sketched three reservation paths below along with assumptions and an initial cost band. Attached: capacity_model_v2.xlsx (detailed QPS->GPU mapping) and neurahealth_cost_estimate_Q4Q1.pdf (pricing bands).

Quick assumptions we used:~
- Baseline per-GPU throughput (H100 80GB, Redwood runtime, int8 + kernel optimizations): ~250 short-request QPS per GPU at p95 ~120ms with KV/prefix caching and 2-request batching average.
- Long-context work (16k-32k) reduces throughput by ~6-8x depending on sequence length; we route those to a smaller pool sized for latency-tolerant traffic.
- Autoscaling / burst: we separate committed pool (min guaranteed) and burst pool (best-effort subject to capacity). Burst is priced lower for on-demand minutes but not SLA-backed.

Option A — Conservative Baseline (low initial commit)~
- Committed: 12 H100 GPUs (guaranteed) across 3 nodes (4 GPUs/node).~
- Expected steady throughput covered: ~3,000 short-request QPS (headroom for baseline + 15% growth).~
- Burst/on-demand buffer: +8 GPUs for spikes (no SLA).~
- Ramp: immediate commit, scale +4 GPUs at month 3 and +4 GPUs at month 6 if usage trends.
- Monthly committed cost (estimate): $120k–$150k.

Option B — Staircase / Phased Ramp (recommended for predictable economics)~
- Committed: 20 H100 GPUs initially across 5 nodes (4 GPUs/node).~
- Canary month 1: use 6 GPUs of the committed pool as a canary with traffic split 10% to canary.
- Ramp schedule: start 20 GPUs month 1; +8 GPUs month 2; +8 GPUs month 4 (total 36 GPUs by month 4) conditioned on usage triggers (SLO attainment and token volume).~
- Burst: +12 GPUs for on-demand bursting with automatic fallback to smaller model variant if saturated.
- Monthly committed cost: $200k–$300k depending on node mix and discount tier.

Option C — Frontloaded Aggressive (fast scale, lower unit price)~
- Committed: 40 H100 GPUs initially to cover projected 6–9 month growth with heavy tails.
- Burst: +20 GPUs.
- Ramp: frontloaded (all committed immediately).
- Monthly committed cost: $380k–$500k.

Operational notes:~
- We recommend the Staircase approach (Option B) for a balance of cost predictability and safety. The canary month gives NeuraHealth an opportunity to validate latency and routing policies before larger ramp steps.
- For long-context workloads, we propose a dedicated lane sized at 6–8 GPUs initially with separate autoscaling policies to avoid noisy neighbor effects.
- We can provide SLA-backed Dedicated capacity for the committed GPUs and best-effort capacity for burst.

Next steps we suggest:~
1) Review the attached capacity model to confirm traffic distribution assumptions.
2) If Option B looks good, we’ll turn this into a short SOW (I attached a draft redwood_staircase_sow_draft.pdf) and a DocuSign link for signatures.
3) Technical kickoff with Karthik and Lauren to finalize runtime knobs (shards, cache sizes, quantization).

I’m happy to hop on a 30m call tomorrow to walk through the numbers.

—
Aditya Rao

Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity sizing for predictive API

Quick technical notes to supplement Aditya's options (attached runtime_profile_notes.txt):

- Short-request path: we expect ~220–260 short-request QPS per H100 GPU under conservative batching assumptions (1.8 avg batch). If you can tolerate slightly higher avg batch (2.5), throughput rises ~25%.
- Long-context: for 16k–32k requests, shard the model across 2–3 processes with KV caching; expect 30–40 QPS per GPU depending on decode length. Recommend isolating long-context to 6 GPUs initially.
- Cache sizing: allocate ~48–64GB KV cache capacity per GPU for prefix caching on high-frequency queries — that materially lowers token compute for repeated prompts.
- Quantization: int8 recommended for short requests where model quality impact is negligible; for long-context or sensitive outputs, prefer fp16 path.
- Autoscaling policy: trigger scale-up at sustained 80% GPU utilization over 5 minutes; scale-down at <50% for 10 minutes. Recommend conservative cooldowns to avoid oscillation for NeuraHealth's traffic patterns.

Proposed month-by-month committed GPU allocation if you take Option B (Staircase):~
- Month 0 (canary): 20 committed (6 used for canary lane, 14 routing capacity); 6 GPUs long-context pool dedicated.
- Month 1: +8 GPUs -> 28 committed (8 additional to absorb growth).
- Month 3: +8 GPUs -> 36 committed.
- Month 6: evaluate and add +4–8 GPUs if forecast holds.

I attached a short runtime profile and test-plan that we typically run during canary (latency sweeps, burst tests, failure injection). Happy to run those with your infra team during the canary window.

-Karthik
Principal Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference
karthik@redwood.inference

Aditya / Karthik — this looks solid. Procurement is comfortable presenting the Staircase option to the finance committee as long as we get:
- A clear canary plan for month 0 with acceptance criteria (SLOs, traffic split, success metrics).
- A simple exit clause if latency regressions >10% on p95 during the canary.
- A one-page cost-to-value summary comparing Option A vs B vs C.

If you can send the SOW and the DocuSign link, we can try to get approvals on a 2-week cadence. Also confirm whether the committed GPUs can be redistributed across AZs in our cloud region — we prefer multi-AZ placement for resilience.

Thanks — copying Procurement who will coordinate PO details.

Best,
Elliot

Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity sizing for predictive API — next steps and SOW

Elliot — great, thanks. Summary and agreed next steps below:~

Agreed plan: Option B (Staircase) with canary month.
- Committed GPUs: start at 20 H100s (5 nodes, 4GPUs/node).
- Dedicated long-context lane: 6 GPUs.
- Canary: month 0, route 10% traffic to canary subset (6 GPUs). Acceptance criteria: p95 latency for short-requests <= 150ms, 99% success rate for model responses, no more than 10% degradation vs demo baseline. If acceptance fails, rollback to baseline routing and no further ramp.
- Ramp: +8 GPUs at month 2, +8 GPUs at month 4 (36 total by month 4) subject to usage and SLO checks.
- Multi-AZ: yes, committed GPUs can be distributed across up to 2 AZs in your preferred region; we’ll provide AZ placement options in the SOW.

SOW / procurement: I attached redwood_staircase_sow_draft.pdf and included a DocuSign link for the current draft: https://www.docusign.net/sign/XYZ-NEU-2026-042. HubSpot deal: https://app.hubspot.com/deal/1234567 (NEU-2026-042).

Next steps / owners:~

- NeuraHealth Procurement: review PO terms and confirm legal; target signature by 2027-01-28.
- Karthik + Lauren: schedule technical kickoff and canary test-plan (next week).
- Finance: finalize discount tier upon signed commitment.

If Procurement wants a single-page cost comparison, I’ll send that Monday morning. Thanks everyone — happy to coordinate a short call to finalize SOW questions.
